sentences.text: Plesiotylosaurus means "near Tylosaurus" and is an extinct genus of marine lizard in the mosasaur family.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — has a lower jaw measuring 98 cm, suggesting the animal reached an estimated length of about 6 meters.
The genus Plesiotylosaurus was named by Camp in 1942.
A 2009 study by Lindgren analyzed the cranial osteology of Plesiotylosaurus using the holotype skull LACM 2759 and specimen UCMP 137249.
Plesiotylosaurus had elongated jaws and a robust skull similar to Prognathodon, indicating a distinct prey preference.
The animal possessed a solid bony rostrum, a wide internarial bar, a long maxillo-premaxillary suture, an overlapping postorbitofrontal process, and a long narrow anterior mandibular channel.
Lindgren identified the shared cranial characteristics between Plesiotylosaurus and Tylosaurinae as an example of convergent evolution.
Plesiotylosaurus is most frequently classified as a mosasaurine mosasaur closely related to the genus Prognathodon.
The parent group of Plesiotylosaurus is the subfamily Mosasaurinae.
Plesiotylosaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
Plesiotylosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
Fossils of Plesiotylosaurus were found in the Middle Maastrichtian Moreno Formation in California.
Plesiotylosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
